purpose: Test a causally independent, gold-specific Asian-session compression -> London expansion entry source with natural one-trade-per-day density under the frozen 30-second lifecycle.

source_basis.logic: Gold-specific public indicator builds 00:00-06:00 overnight range, waits for breakout until 10:00, one trade/day maximum; published author reports XAUUSD M15 use.
Gold-specific public EA measures Asian range and trades whichever side breaks during London using OCO logic.

source_basis.source: TradingView GOLD Asian Range Breakout Signals
source_basis.logic: Open-source gold script confirms London breakouts relative to Asian high/low; supports completed-close semantics.

frozen_common.range_price: P75 Bid high/low formed only from ticks in the completed 00:00-06:00 UTC interval
frozen_common.ownership: one accepted source trade per UTC day maximum; first chronological side wins; no rearm
frozen_common.spread_gate: <=25 P75 points at executable entry tick
frozen_common.lifecycle: 0.01 lot; $0.30 stop; +$0.10 trail activation; $0.03 trail distance; 30s max hold; $0.02 round-trip commission
frozen_common.breakout_buffer: ZERO_BUFFER_CAUSAL_BASELINE because public pages expose configurable buffer but no unambiguous broker-independent default

configs.C01_FIRST_STRICT_TICK: First P75 Bid tick strictly above Asian high => BUY, or strictly below Asian low => SELL.
configs.C02_FIRST_COMPLETED_S5_CLOSE: First completed causal S5 bar in breakout window closing strictly beyond Asian high/low; enter first executable tick at/after bar edge if still beyond.
configs.C03_FIRST_COMPLETED_S15_CLOSE: Same as C02 using S15 completed close; faster than source M15 chart but remains within frozen short-horizon research while testing close confirmation.

selection_rule: Advance only a config that passes all supply/economic prescreen gates; prefer higher direct net, then more official wins, then more accepted trades. No post-result semantic or numeric rescue.
forbidden: range-width fitting or 300-2000 point filter until broker-point semantics are independently normalized
